page: Microsoft Azure E8-4as_v5 is an EASv5-family virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled at 2 threads per core. The memory configuration is highly dense, providing 64.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 16.0 GB per core. It has no bundled local storage but is Premium Storage capable, and does not include a GPU or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, scoring 2701.19 in stress-ng single-core tests, placing it in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 5398.78 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 3636.0, both falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is mixed: read-only large block bandwidth is average at 39.23 GB/sec, while write bandwidth for large blocks is weak at 22.78 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET performance also rank in the bottom 25%, reflecting constraints under parallelized workloads.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:16, the E8-4as_v5 offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel processing power. The trade-off is clear: strong single-threaded execution coupled with massive RAM capacity, but limited multi-core scaling. This makes it suitable for memory-heavy, low-concurrency applications, small-scale caching layers, light database workloads, or single-threaded data processing tasks.
